title: Francis Needham to Walsingham, 28 July 1587, BL Harley MS 287 ff. 39-40 (DECODE R8479)

steps.what: Fetched the four page images of R8479 from DECODE with the session cookie.
Identified f. 39v as the cipher page; box-shaped signs with dots below or inside; glosses advise, enemyes, campe nor the towne.
Gloss-to-sign alignment gave e, n, o, r, s, t, h, w, m, a, d, v, i, y; showed that dot position (below vs inside) distinguishes letters.
CSP Foreign vol. 21 pt 3: Needham's same-day SP 84 despatch (pp. 206-8) and the note that Needham used Wilkes's cipher, key in Add MS 5935.
Searched Cryptiana (elizabeth.htm) and the web for the Wilkes key.
Two subagents transcribed lines A-E and F-I; the second stopped early when image reading timed out.
Line A read 'want of intelligence', line D 'whether there was any bridge'; recognised the alphabet runs a-i, k-s, t-z through the three grids.
Read lines F, G, H on 2x crops with the full key: channel closed with hoys and flyboats fastened with chains, strengthened behind with flat boats.
Content matches the calendared same-day despatch (bridge across the haven of Sluys, fireship).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Contemporary interlinear glosses on the same pages ('advise', 'enemyes', 'campe nor the towne', 'Burgrave') gave most letter values, and the alphabetical layout of the three-grid pigpen fixed the rest.
outcome.notes: Every cipher run of f. 39v read; the f. 39r/40r runs were glossed at the time. fraction_read = decoded signs / all signs of the six unglossed runs in cipher.txt (182/186); glossed words excluded.

prior.where: Contemporary glosses decipher a few words and the f. 39r runs; the key is said to survive in BL Add MS 5935 (CSP Foreign 21/3 p. 35 n. 4). The long f. 39v runs had no decipherment found.
